title: Adaptive rollouts — console flow proposals and wireframe notes
content:
Context
------
Working notes for an adaptive rollouts flow that supports: lightweight canaries, user-defined A/B experiments, and automatic fallback policies when downstream model variants fail SLAs. These are intentionally product-proposal-level sketches — meant to seed engineering/Design/SE grooming.

Goals (high-level)
- Make it easy to create a canary with minimal fields: target traffic %, success metric, duration.
- Enable A/B experiments where variants can be multi-model and multi-config (quantization, routing tier).
- Provide automatic fallback rules that are predictable and auditable; ensure visibility into why a fallback happened.
- Keep controls composable so teams can use hosted, dedicated, or private deployments without changing UI mental model.

Audience
- Primary: product/platform engineers who own inference routes.
- Secondary: SRE/ops on-call, solutions engineers running customer rollouts.

Top-level console pages proposed
1) Rollout Overview (list) — shows active/past rollouts, quick status, small sparkline of latency/error, primary metric, owner, created_at. Quick actions: pause, promote, abort, snapshot.
2) Create rollout (wizard + JSON toggle) — two modes: quick-create (guided fields) and advanced (full JSON).
3) Rollout detail — timeline, live metrics, request samples, variant breakdown, rollback reasons, audit log.
4) Fallback policies — a global library of policies that can be attached to a rollout or route.

Quick-create wireframe notes (step-by-step)
- Step 1: Name + route + owner + purpose (free text)
- Step 2: Variant selection (card deck): choose base model + variant overrides (quant, batch config, region). Each variant has a compact perf profile (latency/cost/accuracy heuristics). "Add variant" button.
- Step 3: Traffic plan: slider or numeric for allocation. Default: canary 5% -> auto-increase to 20% over 30m if success. Editable schedule.
- Step 4: Success criteria: pre-set templates (latency P95 < X ms; error rate < Y; quality regression < Z using eval set) or custom metric (link to console metrics).
- Step 5: Fallback policy attach: choose from library or inline rule.
- Step 6: Review & create (summary panel on right with cost estimate, expected throughput, and what happens on failure).

Wireframe interactions (notes for Design)
- Traffic slider should show both % and expected qps for the current route (estimated).
- Variant cards show three small badges: est-latency, est-cost, est-quality. Hover for details.
- Inline small text showing which infra (hosted/dedicated/private) variant will land on. If mismatched infra, show warning but allow proceed (with note).
- JSON toggle opens full rollout config in side panel; edits sync to wizard fields.

Rollout detail page — key panels
- Top bar: title, status pill (Running/Paused/Failed/Completed), start & owner info, quick action buttons (pause/promote/abort/restart).
- Left column: timeline with state transitions + annotations (auto-promote at 30m, fallback triggered at 12:02). Each event links to audit log + request examples.
- Center: live metrics stream (P50/P95 latency, errors, tokens/sec, success metric). Small timeline scrubber to inspect previous windows.
- Right: variant table with traffic %, success metric by variant, per-variant logs (sample requests and responses), and per-variant cost.
- Bottom: fallback policy joined view, with last trigger event and last execution reason.

Automatic fallback policies — UX patterns
- Library concept: create once, reuse many times. Policy fields (flat): trigger conditions (latency threshold, error-rate threshold, SLA miss count, model crash count), cool-down period, fallback target (default variant, degrade to cheaper quantized model, route to region-fallback), notify (pager/team slack).
- Execution preview: in the create flow show a simulation for the past 24h based on metrics — "This policy would have fired N times" (approx).
- Policy audit trail: every policy decision must be recorded with metric deltas and the decision tree snapshot. Include a link to raw metric time-series for later debug.

A/B experiments notes (differences from canary)
- Must allow multiple variants >2 (e.g., control + 3 treatments).
- Built-in statistical guardrails: choose test duration, minimum sample size, stopping rules (early stop for significance or futility).
- Exposure controls: deterministic assignment by user_id hash or random sampling. Exportable result summary with confidence intervals and recommended winner.
- UI: a results tab with visuals (lift bars, p-values, confidence intervals) and a recommended action (promote winner, continue test, abort).

Backlog grooming (tickets, rough priority)
- HIGH: basic wizard + rollout detail UI (JIRA-4521) — MVP for internal teams; include traffic slider, variants, attach policy. (owner: Leah).
- MED: fallback policy library & execution preview (JIRA-4522) — needs metric simulator and policy engine hooks. (owner: Rajesh).
- MED: A/B experiment analytics UI (JIRA-4523) — backend for significance computation + results export. (owner: Marta).
- LOW: per-variant request inspector with redaction rules & sample export (JIRA-4524) — privacy review. (owner: Diego).
- TECHDEBT: unify rollout JSON schema with private deploy API (JIRA-4525).

Acceptance criteria (MVP)
- Users can create a canary rollout with 2 variants, set traffic %, and start/pause/abort.
- Rollout detail shows traffic split and live P95 latency by variant.
- A fallback policy can be attached and will surface last trigger event in the UI.
- All actions are logged in audit with actor and timestamp.

Open questions / risks
- How do we surface cost tradeoffs without scaring teams? (show "expected incremental cost" and a small tooltip).
- Are we comfortable with rollouts attaching cross-deployment variants (hosted <-> private)? If allowed, need tighter access controls and warnings.
- Metric alignment: what metric sources are canonical for rollout decisions (console metrics vs. customer-provided probes)?
- For A/B, do we expose raw p-values or a more product-friendly "confidence" label?

Notes-to-self (informal)
- Prioritize a simple happy-path wizard first. Complex schedulers come later.
- Build a mock with 3 real customer routes for usability testing.
- Check with Privacy about sample request inspector scope.

Sketch (textual)
[Create rollout wizard — two-column layout]
Left: stepper (1-6). Right: live summary card with small cost estimate, risk signal (green/yellow/red).

Timeline example text entry:
- 10:00 create canary 5% (auto-increase to 30% over 1h)
- 10:30 auto-promote to 30% (metric OK)
- 11:02 fallback triggered -> route traffic to current default, notify #oncall

Prototype tasks for next sprint
- Design: high-fidelity for the quick-create wizard + rollout detail (2 screens)
- Eng: backend endpoints for create/list/detail + attach policy (mock impl)
- Data: define metric contract and sample ingestion for simulation
- SE: prepare doc for enterprise customers about cross-deployment rollouts

References and inspiration
- Existing internal rollout API spec (CONFLUENCE-1234)
- Google Cloud traffic splitting UX (notes copied into figma)
- Internal SRE postmortem: rollout-fallback-case-2024 (lessons for audit)

End of notes.
